releases.name: 3.0.0: one entry point, one reference
releases.notes:
## Install

Minimal package: `opencode-go-model-picker-3.0.0-min.zip` contains only what the skill runs — `SKILL.md`, `references/` (one doc plus two dated seeds), `scripts/` (one entry point + modules) and `LICENSE`. Unzip it into `~/.config/opencode/skills/` so the folder is named `opencode-go-model-picker`. Verify with `node scripts/go.mjs --help` (four verbs: `run` / `report` / `check` / `apply`).

Full notes: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/sogeisetsu/opencode-go-model-picker/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) · 中文：[CHANGELOG-ZH.md](https://github.com/sogeisetsu/opencode-go-model-picker/blob/main/zh/CHANGELOG-ZH.md)

## [3.0.0] - 2026-11-01

### The size of the simplification

3.0.0 is not a feature release: it is the same job described with **an order of
magnitude less text**. Measured against the 2.0.0 tag:

| What the model must read | 2.0.0 | 3.0.0 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Markdown files | 7 (`SKILL.md` + 6 references) | 2 (`SKILL.md` + `plan-facts.md`) | −5 files |
| Characters | 104,181 | 8,291 | **12.6× smaller** (−92%) |
| Lines | 1,776 | 168 | **10.6× fewer** (−91%) |
| Estimated tokens | ≈27,400 | ≈2,200 | **≈25,200 saved per full read** |
| `SKILL.md` alone | 18,804 chars ≈4,900 tok | 4,221 chars ≈1,100 tok | −78% |
| Runnable entry points | 9 runtime scripts (11 with maintainer tools) | 1 (`go.mjs`) | −8 runtime |
| Minimal install zip | 128,802 B | 89,163 B | −31% |

A typical 2.0.0 run loaded `SKILL.md` plus two or three references (≈11–15k
tokens); the same run now loads 8.3k characters, about 2.2k tokens — roughly
**80–85% less context** before any work starts. Token figures are estimates at
3.8 characters/token (no tokenizer ships with the repo); character and line counts
are exact: `git show v2.0.0:SKILL.md | wc -c` and the same for each reference.

Code did not shrink — it moved: ~4,700 lines of scripts became ~5,300 lines of
modules plus tests, because the rules that used to be prose (refresh order, basis
selection, priced columns, chain shape, apply diff) are now enforced by code.

### Breaking

- **One entry point.** `scripts/go.mjs` replaces nine scripts — `discover-agents`,
 `probe-console`, `calibrate-usage`, `quota-math`, `refresh-snapshot`,
 `refresh-prices`, `refresh-scores`, `snapshot-summary` and `fetch-go-models` are
 gone. Four verbs: `run` (agents → Console → usage → refresh → plan diff → basis,
 one serial pass, one `run.json`), `report` (table, money columns, config blocks),
 `check` (the gate before delivery), `apply` (exact diff; writes only with
 `--write`, only the named file, only that agent's `model` value).
- **One reference.** `references/plan-facts.md` replaces `quota-math.md`,
 `model-snapshot.md`, `data-sources.md`, `agent-sources.md`, `console-mcp.md` and
 `output-format.md`. `SKILL.md` drops from ~19k to ~4k characters and is
 model-facing only; teaching moved to the READMEs.
- **Code over prose.** The refresh order (three writers, one snapshot file), the
 `Basis:` line and its denominator, the priced `$/session` column, chain-shape
 rules, seed staleness, mode resolution and the apply diff are computed, not
 described. The nine self-checks became `go.mjs check`.
- `apply` refuses a chain containing a dead id and refuses to write a result that
 does not re-parse.

### Added

- `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` (built-in `node:test`, no dependencies):
 `tests/golden/` holds outputs captured from the 2.0.0 scripts and covers pricing,
 discovery and the five Console states; CLI tests cover offline degradation, the
 report gate, and dry-run versus `--write`.
- `run --offline` always produces a dated, seed-labelled `run.json`; `data.quality`
 says `live` / `seed` / `none` instead of leaving the reader to infer it.

### Changed

- `scripts/check-docs.mjs` and `scripts/generate-assets.mjs` moved to `tools/`:
 they maintain the repository, not the skill, and are not part of the minimal
 install.
- Moved `test-prompts.json` to `tests/prompts.json` and documented it in the
 repository layout: it is an evaluation fixture (a request paired with the
 behaviour the skill must exhibit), not a runtime asset — nothing loads it.

releases.name: v1.2.0
releases.notes:
# v1.2.0

`skill_management` gives every installed OpenCode skill a switch: list what is installed, find out
why one will not load, hide it from the model, and put it back. Disabling writes **one** global
`skill` permission rule — no skill file is ever moved, edited or deleted.

**No breaking changes in 1.2.0.** The four actions, their inputs, the JSON envelope, the written
rule shape, the same-line marker and the single-file layout are unchanged since 1.1.0.

## Fixed since v1.1.0

- **`list` no longer reports "N skills differ across other agents" on every call.**
 `summary.diverged` counted hidden internal agents (`title`, `summary`, …), which carry
 `{*,*,deny}`; on a real machine that made every skill look divergent (33/33) and added a noise
 warning to each `list`. Only **visible** agents are compared now; `inspect.agents[]` still lists
 every agent, so the detail is not lost.
- **Frontmatter booleans no longer contradict each other.** `disable-model-invocation: "false"` is a
 string, and `Boolean("false") === true`, so `inspect` reported it as `true` while `list` reported
 `autoinvoke: false` for the same file. `true/yes/on/1` and `false/no/off/0` (quoted or not) are
 normalized now, and both fields go through the same rule.
- **A failed sidecar write no longer turns a successful config change into an error.** Once the
 config was written and verified, a sidecar write failure used to surface as `internal_error`: the
 file really changed, but the result had no `changed` / `diff`. It now returns `ok: true`,
 `changed: true`, keeps `diff`, sets `sidecar: null`, and explains itself in `warnings`. The config
 change is not rolled back.
- **`enable` is no longer blocked by an unrelated file's syntax error.** It reads sidecar-recorded
 config files alongside the target; before, any of them failing to parse plus "no candidate rule"
 produced `config_unparsable`. The hard refusal now applies only to the **target** config file;
 other files are reported in `warnings` by name.

## Also since v1.1.0

- **The installer checks before writing.** If `opencode.json(c)` already lists this package in
 `plugins`, or a second copy sits in `plugins/`, it refuses and exits with code `2`, leaving every
 file untouched — two sources make the host report `Duplicate plugin ID` and fail one of them.
- New installer flags: `--check` / `--dry-run`, `--uninstall` (deletes only this plugin's file),
 `--npm` (asserts the npm channel, never writes), `--force`, `--json`. `<config>` resolves the way
 the host resolves it (`$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` first).
- The plugin exports `PLUGIN_VERSION`, asserted against `package.json` by the harness.
- The acceptance harness grew from 260 to **326 assertions**, and now validates every action's
 `output` against the declared JSON Schema (required fields, property types, `error.code` /
 `error.message`) and asserts that `content` is the same data as `output`.
- README is down to 51 lines; field tables, installer flags, package contents, usage and the test
 workflow moved to the documentation site.
- The documentation site gained **Design decisions** (why permission rules instead of policies, why
 there is no `allow`, why global-only, why text edits plus a same-line marker, why the sidecar is
 only an audit trail — each with its cost) and **Development & verification** (harness sections,
 CI, the performance and release gates, npm package contents, why two copies cannot coexist).
 The **Permissions** page now expands Effects into a `deny` vs `ask` comparison with three real
 skill examples. English and Chinese stay mirrored.

## What it does

| Action | What you get | Writes config |
|---|---|---|
| `list` | Every registered skill and its effective state for the **calling agent** (`available` / `disabled` / `ask`) | No |
| `inspect` | Why one skill is (not) usable: the matched rule, per-agent differences, how the id was derived | No |
| `disable` | Hidden from the model-visible list and rejected at load (`effect: "ask"` keeps it listed with confirmation) | Yes |
| `enable` | Deletes the one blocking rule, whoever wrote it | Yes |

Permissions are evaluated for the **calling agent only**: last match wins (`findLast`, with `*`
and `?` globs), and **no match falls back to `ask`, not `allow`**.

The rule `disable` writes is exactly this line (the trailing comment is the provenance marker
`enable` uses):

```jsonc
{ "action": "skill", "resource": "windows-shell", "effect": "deny" } // skill_management
```

Writes are atomic, preserve indentation, key order, line endings (CRLF/LF) and BOM, keep one
backup, and are verified by reloading the host and polling the caller's rule set; a write the host
did not pick up is rolled back.

## Usage

```text
skill_management({ action: "list" })
skill_management({ action: "inspect", id: "windows-shell" })
skill_management({ action: "disable", id: "windows-shell" })
skill_management({ action: "disable", id: "windows-shell", dryRun: true })
skill_management({ action: "disable", id: "windows-shell", effect: "ask" })
skill_management({ action: "enable", id: "windows-shell" })
```

Full field tables and error codes are on the four action pages of the docs site:
<https://sogeisetsu.github.io/opencode-skill-management/>

## Install

| Channel | Command / asset | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **npm (recommended)** | `opencode plugin add opencode-skill-management@1.2.0` | Installs the package and registers it in the global config; no token needed |
| git spec | `opencode plugin add github:sogeisetsu/opencode-skill-management` | Bypasses the npm registry |
| Single file | asset `skill_management.js` | Drop it into `<config>/plugins/`; best for offline use |
| npm tarball | asset `opencode-skill-management-1.2.0.tgz` | The same tarball npm publishes; for auditing or internal mirrors |

Verify it loaded in a **new process**:

```pwsh
opencode plugin list --builtin
# skill_management 1.2.0 opencode-skill-management@1.2.0
```

## Compatibility and verification…

en.headline: 27 own commits plus 23 automated commits across five repositories
en.summary: **27 own commits** were recorded across five repositories, plus 23 automated commits by `github-actions[bot]`. In `sogeisetsu/opencode-skill-management`, 16 commits covered releases `v1.2.0` and `1.2.1`, serialized write enable/disable behavior, target-only rejection of unparsable configs, output-schema validation, and documentation-site updates. In `sogeisetsu/opencode-go-model-picker`, 6 commits introduced a single `scripts/go.mjs` entry point with four verbs, corrected release measurements, and removed two test artifacts. The 2 commits in `sogeisetsu/opencode-agent-sandbox` documented `knowledge-ingest` verification and the roles of three review commands, while 2 commits in `sogeisetsu/sopen-translate` corrected G2 status and documented the Google 2 key path. The remaining own commit in `sogeisetsu/sogeisetsu` added a generated-artifact validation gate to the daily report workflow.

releaseNotes.summary: This release replaces nine runtime scripts with the single `scripts/go.mjs` entry point offering `run`, `report`, `check`, and `apply`, and consolidates six reference documents into `references/plan-facts.md`. It is a breaking change that reduces the model-facing text from 104,181 to 8,291 characters and the minimal install zip from 128,802 to 89,163 bytes, while moving rules such as refresh order, basis selection, pricing, and apply diffs into code. It adds `node:test` coverage with golden outputs, makes `run --offline` produce a dated seed-labelled `run.json` with explicit `data.quality`, and moves repository maintenance scripts into `tools/`.

This release fixes `list` counting hidden internal agents as divergent, normalizes frontmatter booleans so `inspect` and `list` agree, and reports sidecar write failures as successful config changes with warnings instead of `internal_error`. `enable` now hard-refuses only when the target config file is unparsable, while unrelated files are listed in warnings. It also adds installer flags `--check`, `--dry-run`, `--uninstall`, `--npm`, `--force`, and `--json`, expands the acceptance harness to 326 assertions with output-schema validation, and adds Design decisions and Development & verification documentation pages.

zh.headline: 27 次本人提交，另有 23 次自动提交，覆盖五个仓库
zh.summary: 当天在五个仓库产生 **27 次本人提交**，另有 23 次由 `github-actions[bot]` 自动提交。`sogeisetsu/opencode-skill-management` 的 16 次提交涵盖 `v1.2.0` 与 `1.2.1` 发布、写入启停的串行化、仅针对目标配置拒绝不可解析配置、输出结构校验及文档站更新。`sogeisetsu/opencode-go-model-picker` 的 6 次提交引入带四个动词的单一 `scripts/go.mjs` 入口，修正发布测量数据并删除两个测试产物。`sogeisetsu/opencode-agent-sandbox` 的 2 次提交记录了 `knowledge-ingest` 验证流程和三种审查命令的分工，`sogeisetsu/sopen-translate` 的 2 次提交修正 G2 状态并说明 Google 2 密钥路径。`sogeisetsu/sogeisetsu` 剩余的 1 次本人提交为日报工作流加入生成物校验门禁。

releaseNotes.summary: 该版本以单一 `scripts/go.mjs` 入口取代九个运行时脚本，提供 `run`、`report`、`check`、`apply` 四个动词，并将六份参考文档合并为 `references/plan-facts.md`。这是一次破坏性变更，模型需阅读的文本从 104,181 字符降至 8,291 字符，最小安装包从 128,802 字节降至 89,163 字节，同时把刷新顺序、基准选择、定价和 apply 差异等规则移入代码。新版本加入基于 `node:test` 的黄金输出测试，使 `run --offline` 生成带日期和种子标记的 `run.json` 并明确 `data.quality`，还将仓库维护脚本移至 `tools/`。

该版本修复 `list` 把隐藏内部代理计为差异项的问题，统一规范化 frontmatter 布尔值，使 `inspect` 与 `list` 结果一致，并在 sidecar 写入失败时以警告报告成功的配置变更而非 `internal_error`。`enable` 现在仅在目标配置文件不可解析时硬拒绝，其他文件按名称列入警告。新增安装器参数 `--check`、`--dry-run`、`--uninstall`、`--npm`、`--force`、`--json`，验收测试扩充至 326 项断言并校验输出结构，文档站新增 Design decisions 与 Development & verification 页面。
